    Getting Started with hexmakR

    Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
    getting-started.Rmd

    Installation

    Install the development package from GitHub:

    # install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("CTTIR/hexmakR")

    Start with a fresh logo 

    library(hexmakR)
design <- logo_design("My package")

    This creates a hexagonal frame and name with no archived scientific motif. The name sits inside the lower part of the frame. A pentagon or square is available with shape = "pentagon" or shape = "square".

    Add your own artwork as individually editable parts:

    design <- hex_add_part(design, "circle", x = .5, y = .6, r = .15)
design <- hex_add_part(design, "line",
                       x = c(.3, .7), y = c(.6, .6), col = "white", lwd = 3)
hex_layers(design)
#>           id     type    fill     col points  role   name visible
#> 1 layer_0001  polygon #191919 #000000      6 frame  Frame    TRUE
#> 2 layer_0002 pathgrob #FFFFFF    <NA>   1265  name   Name    TRUE
#> 3  part_0001   circle #009E73 #FFFFFF      1 added Circle    TRUE
#> 4  part_0002    lines #009E73   white      2 added   Line    TRUE
print(design)

    Parts have stable IDs such as part_0001. The native frame and name have layer_ IDs. Obtain the current IDs from hex_layers() before editing.

    design <- hex_edit_layer(design, "part_0001", fill = "#45B59A", dx = .04)
design <- hex_duplicate_part(design, "part_0001")
design <- hex_edit_layer(design, "part_0003", dx = -.2, scale = .7)

    Use an icon or archive artwork

    All 46 generic icons remain available:

    logo_design("Study", shape = "square", icon = "microscope")

    Archive reuse is optional. Add selected artwork to the design you are making:

    head(hex_catalog())
#>          name        repo   family      symbol      kind
#> 1    molpathR    molpathR clinical    molpathR R package
#> 2      pressR      pressR clinical      pressR R package
#> 3     scimagR     scimagR clinical     scimagR R package
#> 4 zhncommandR zhncommandR clinical zhncommandR R package
#> 5  brainwritR  brainwritR evidence  brainwritR R package
#> 6     delphyr     delphyR evidence     delphyr R package
#>                                                                    source
#> 1                 https://github.com/CTTIR/molpathR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 2                   https://github.com/CTTIR/pressR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 3                  https://github.com/CTTIR/scimagR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 4              https://github.com/CTTIR/zhncommandR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 5               https://github.com/CTTIR/brainwritR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 6 https://github.com/CTTIR/delphyR/blob/main/packages/delphyr/DESCRIPTION
#>     asset_dir
#> 1    molpathR
#> 2      pressR
#> 3     scimagR
#> 4 zhncommandR
#> 5  brainwritR
#> 6     delphyr
design <- hex_reuse_part(design, "phenoscapR")

    This imports the source motif’s editable parts while retaining your name, frame, palette and existing parts. An explicit hex_design("phenoscapR") instead starts from that whole archived design. A call to hex_design() without a package also starts fresh; logo_design("My package") is the direct way to set your own project name.

    Save and continue later

    Use hex_import_art(design, "figure.png") to add an embedded PNG/JPEG image, or supply an SVG file for separately editable vector shapes. Supported SVG curves become vector polylines. The editor provides the same feature under Add an image or vector drawing. Uploads are capped at 10 MiB; outline text and flatten gradients, masks or intersecting clips first. See ?hex_import_art for the supported SVG subset. Item labels and groups can be organised with hex_label_layer() and hex_group_layers().

    hex_save_design(design, "my-package.json")
restored <- hex_read_design("my-package.json")
hex_export(restored, "my-package.svg")
hex_export(restored, "my-package.png", width = 1600)
hex_export(restored, "my-package.pdf")
hex_recipe(restored, "reproduce.R")

    PNG has a transparent exterior. SVG and PDF contain native vector artwork and outlined name glyphs, so they do not depend on locally installed fonts. JSON stores validated settings and parts; opening a project does not evaluate R code. A project must fit within the same 20 MiB limit when saved and reopened.

    Open the manual editor 

    hexmakr_app()

    The Designer opens a new logo. Add parts, select one, and use Apply part edit after changing its colours, position, size, opacity or points. Click a part to select it and drag it to move it. Rename items, organise groups and switch the mouse target to move a whole group together. The CTTIR Gallery tab is secondary; browsing it leaves the current logo unchanged.

    The original generic sticker interface remains available through hexmakr_app(workspace = "classic"). Its hex_sticker() function returns a ggplot object and supports 28 themes, led by the nine CTTIR v5 families, font choices including the bundled JetBrains Mono, and uploaded images.

    See vignette("cttir-library") for archive reuse and editable projects, and vignette("shiny-app") for the manual workflow.
